    12	Formalized (same assumptions, and more general):
    13	* `phase_bessel`: for any measure space `(X, μ)`, any complete complex inner
    14	  product space `H`, any finite index types `ι` (the family index `k`) and `J`
    15	  (the vector index `j`; the TeX has `J = Fin 2`), an orthonormal family
    16	  `u : ι → J → X → ℂ` in `L²(X; ℂ^J)` and `g : J → X → H` with every `g j` in
    17	  `L²`, the integrands `η ↦ ∑ j, u k j η • g j η` and `η ↦ ∑ j, ‖g j η‖²` are
    18	  integrable (the TeX's "the Bochner integrals exist") and
    19	  `∑ k, ‖∫ ∑ j, u k j • g j‖² ≤ ∫ ∑ j, ‖g j‖²`.
    20	* `phase_bessel_conj`: the same with `conj (u k j)` in place of `u k j`.
    21	* `phase_bessel_paper`: the TeX's statement with its own hypotheses
    22	  (`X = ℝ^d` with Lebesgue measure, `J = Fin 2`, `ι = Fin K`, `H` separable),
    23	  both versions.
    24	
    25	Encoding of the hypotheses. `L²(ℝ^d; ℂ²)` is encoded componentwise: each
    26	`u k j` is `MemLp 2`, and orthonormality is the integral identity
    27	`∫ ∑ j, u k j η * conj (u l j η) dη = δ_{kl}` (`IsOrthonormalL2`), which is the
    28	`L²(ℂ^J)` inner product `⟨u_k, u_l⟩` linear in the first slot. Likewise
    29	`g ∈ L²(ℝ^d; H²)` is `MemLp (g j) 2` for each `j`. Measurability and the
    30	existence of the Bochner integrals, implicit in the TeX, are part of `MemLp`
    31	and of the conclusion respectively.
    32	Junk values: the orthonormality integral cannot be a junk `0`, since
    33	`u k j * conj (u l j)` is integrable for `L²` components (`integrable_mul_of_memLp`);
    34	the integrals in the conclusion are of integrable functions, as the conclusion
    35	states.
    36	
    37	Convention ledger. Mathlib's inner product `inner ℂ x y` is conjugate-linear in
    38	the FIRST slot; the TeX's (`⟨u_k,u_l⟩ = ∫ ∑ u_{k,j} \overline{u_{l,j}}`) is
    39	linear in the first slot. Orthonormality is stated directly as the integral
    40	identity above, so no Mathlib inner product on `L²` is involved in the
    41	hypothesis, and the inequality itself (a statement about norms) does not depend
    42	on the convention.
    43	
    44	Proof route (differs from the TeX). The TeX expands `g` in a countable
    45	orthonormal basis of `H`, applies scalar Bessel coefficientwise and sums with
    46	Parseval and Tonelli; separability of `H` is used only for that basis. Here the
    47	projection argument that the TeX uses for scalar Bessel is run directly in `H`:
    48	with `x k = ∫ ∑ j, u k j • g j` and `φ j η = ∑ k, conj (u k j η) • x k`,
    49	`0 ≤ ∫ ∑ j, ‖g j - φ j‖² = ∫ ∑ j, ‖g j‖² - 2 S + S`, `S = ∑ k, ‖x k‖²`.
    50	No basis, Parseval or separability is needed, so the wrapper carries the TeX's
    51	separability hypothesis unused. No σ-finiteness of `μ` is needed either.
    52	-/

   162	/-- Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality (`L:phase-bessel`, display
   163	`E:phase-bessel`), general form: any measure space `(X, μ)`, any complete
   164	complex inner product space `H` (separability not needed), finite index types
   165	`ι` and `J`. Hypotheses: `u` is orthonormal in `L²(X; ℂ^J)` in the sense of
   166	`IsOrthonormalL2`, and every `g j` is in `L²(X; H)`. Conclusion: the coefficient
   167	integrands and `∑ j, ‖g j‖²` are integrable, and
   168	`∑ k, ‖∫ ∑ j, u k j • g j‖² ≤ ∫ ∑ j, ‖g j‖²`. -/
   169	theorem phase_bessel {u : ι → J → X → ℂ} {g : J → X → H}
   170	    (hu : IsOrthonormalL2 μ u) (hg : ∀ j, MemLp (g j) 2 μ) :
   171	    (∀ k, Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, u k j η • g j η) μ) ∧
   172	      Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
   173	      ∑ k, ‖coeff μ u g k‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ η, ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2 ∂μ := by
   174	  obtain ⟨huL, hon⟩ := hu
   175	  have hint := integrable_coeff_integrand huL hg
   176	  have hG := integrable_sum_norm_sq (μ := μ) hg
   177	  refine ⟨hint, hG, ?_⟩
   178	  set x : ι → H := coeff μ u g with hx
   179	  -- the two complex integrands of the expansion
   180	  set A : X → ℂ := fun η => ∑ k, inner ℂ (x k) (∑ j, u k j η • g j η) with hAdef
   181	  set B : X → ℂ := fun η =>
   182	    ∑ k, ∑ l, (∑ j, u k j η * conj (u l j η)) * inner ℂ (x k) (x l) with hBdef
   183	  have hAint : Integrable A μ :=
   184	    integrable_finsetSum _ fun k _ => (hint k).const_inner (x k)
   185	  have hprod : ∀ k l, Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, u k j η * conj (u l j η)) μ :=
   186	    fun k l => integrable_finsetSum _ fun j _ =>
   187	      integrable_mul_of_memLp (huL k j) (memLp_conj (huL l j))
   188	  have hBint : Integrable B μ :=
   189	    integrable_finsetSum _ fun k _ => integrable_finsetSum _ fun l _ =>
   190	      (hprod k l).mul_const _
   191	  have hAval : ∫ η, A η ∂μ = ∑ k, inner ℂ (x k) (x k) := by
   192	    simp only [hAdef]
   193	    rw [integral_finsetSum _ fun k _ => (hint k).const_inner (x k)]
   194	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
   195	    rw [integral_inner (hint k)]
   196	    rfl
   197	  have hBval : ∫ η, B η ∂μ = ∑ k, inner ℂ (x k) (x k) := by
   198	    simp only [hBdef]
   199	    rw [integral_finsetSum _ fun k _ => integrable_finsetSum _ fun l _ =>
   200	      (hprod k l).mul_const _]
   201	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
   202	    rw [integral_finsetSum _ fun l _ => (hprod k l).mul_const _]
   203	    simp_rw [integral_mul_const, hon]
   204	    simp
   205	  -- pointwise expansion of the residual
   206	  have hexp : ∀ η, ∑ j, ‖g j η - ∑ k, conj (u k j η) • x k‖ ^ 2 =
   207	      ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2 - 2 * RCLike.re (A η) + RCLike.re (B η) :=
   208	    fun η => residual_expand (fun k j => u k j η) (fun j => g j η) x

   217	    rw [map_sum]
   218	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) (x k)

   223	/-- Auxiliary (proof route): the componentwise conjugate of an orthonormal
   224	family is orthonormal (`∫ ∑ conj u_k u_l = conj δ_{kl} = δ_{kl}`). -/
   225	theorem isOrthonormalL2_conj {u : ι → J → X → ℂ} (hu : IsOrthonormalL2 μ u) :
   226	    IsOrthonormalL2 μ (fun k j η => conj (u k j η)) := by
   227	  refine ⟨fun k j => memLp_conj (hu.1 k j), fun k l => ?_⟩
   228	  have h := congrArg conj (hu.2 k l)
   229	  rw [← integral_conj] at h

   236	`\overline{u_{k,j}}` in place of `u_{k,j}`"), general form, with the same
   237	hypotheses as `phase_bessel`: integrability of the conjugated coefficient

   239	`∑ k, ‖∫ ∑ j, conj (u k j) • g j‖² ≤ ∫ ∑ j, ‖g j‖²`. -/
   240	theorem phase_bessel_conj {u : ι → J → X → ℂ} {g : J → X → H}
   241	    (hu : IsOrthonormalL2 μ u) (hg : ∀ j, MemLp (g j) 2 μ) :
   242	    (∀ k, Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, conj (u k j η) • g j η) μ) ∧
   243	      Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
   244	      ∑ k, ‖∫ η, ∑ j, conj (u k j η) • g j η ∂μ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   245	        ∫ η, ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
   246	  phase_bessel (isOrthonormalL2_conj hu) hg

   248	/-- `L:phase-bessel` with the manuscript's own hypotheses
   249	(`notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` 346-355 at 975feb3): `H` a separable
   250	complex Hilbert space, `{u_k}_{k < K}` a finite orthonormal family in
   251	`L²(ℝ^d; ℂ²)` (encoded by `IsOrthonormalL2` on `Rd d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`
   252	with Lebesgue measure `volume`), and `g = (g₁, g₂) ∈ L²(ℝ^d; H²)`. Conclusion:
   253	the Bochner integrals exist (integrability of every integrand) and both
   254	`E:phase-bessel` and its conjugated version hold. The separability hypothesis
   255	`_hsep` is carried for fidelity and unused: the proof needs no basis of `H`. -/
   256	theorem phase_bessel_paper {d K : ℕ}
   257	    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
   258	    (_hsep : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H)
   259	    {u : Fin K → Fin 2 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℂ}
   260	    {g : Fin 2 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → H}
   261	    (hu : IsOrthonormalL2 volume u) (hg : ∀ j, MemLp (g j) 2 volume) :
   262	    (∀ k, Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, u k j η • g j η)) ∧
   263	      (∀ k, Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, conj (u k j η) • g j η)) ∧
   264	      Integrable (fun η => ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2) ∧
   265	      ∑ k, ‖∫ η, ∑ j, u k j η • g j η‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ η, ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2 ∧
   266	      ∑ k, ‖∫ η, ∑ j, conj (u k j η) • g j η‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ η, ∑ j, ‖g j η‖ ^ 2 := by
   267	  obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := phase_bessel hu hg
   268	  obtain ⟨h4, -, h5⟩ := phase_bessel_conj hu hg
   269	  exact ⟨h1, h4, h2, h3, h5⟩
   270

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision 975feb3, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98 and 3920258.
     9	The later revisions changed prose, titles, the literature review, layout and
    10	figures, added a zero-covariance remark after `H:homog` and qualified a strict
    11	comparison in `T:first` (not cited here) as asserted only for nonzero
    12	covariance. Every cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at
    13	3920258 and 975feb3. Between these two revisions every cited lemma,
    14	proposition, theorem and equation has the same statement and proof up to
    15	whitespace and braces, with one exception: the statement of `T:full-upper`
    16	(cited only as not formalized) now ends with a cross-reference to Theorem
    17	`T:intro-upper` instead of Goal `G:upper`, and its mathematics is unchanged.
    18	The cited sections `S:model` (the zero-covariance remark and a roadmap
    19	figure), `S:two-clock-screen` (Goal `G:sharp` renamed Theorem
    20	`T:intro-second-moment` in the prose), `S:temporal-equilibrium` and
    21	`S:intrinsic-white-evaluation` (new attribution paragraphs) changed only in
    22	prose. TeX line numbers were moved to 975feb3 by a line map; each cited range
    23	lies in unchanged text (script checks recorded in
    24	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    25	
    26	## Scope
    27	
    28	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    29	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    30	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    31	  elaborated types.
    32	- The rows cover every public theorem (810) and 162 definitions whose
    33	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    34	  60 public definitions have no rows of their own: 56 (for example
    35	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    36	  statements, and four are the instances that make `TimeCompletion.Pre` a
    37	  pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the Lean source or in
    38	  `Audit/`.
    39	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    40	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    41	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    42	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    43	- The thirty-three `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    44	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    45	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`, and `GaussianTest` is the
    46	  Gaussian-test foundation of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`) model `H:homog` and
    47	  formalize the conclusions of twenty-nine
    48	  labelled results in full. Twenty-six need no supplied input:
    49	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own
    50	  hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    51	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no

    53	  wrappers `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the
    54	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is
    55	  not formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    56	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under
    57	  the full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`
    58	  models clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
    59	  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
    60	  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
    61	  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
    62	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
    63	  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    64	  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's
    65	  hypotheses (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability

   103	  are stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog` with `a = alpha0`,
   104	  the range of `gamma`, and of `beta` for the corollary) by
   105	  `frequency_row_paper` and `frequency_time_paper`, with the constant
   106	  chosen before `d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h`. `L:occupation-kernel-row` and
   107	  `L:spatial-physical-pair` are stated with the section's hypotheses
   108	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `D = q - 2a`) by `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
   109	  and `spatial_physical_pair_paper`. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` is stated

   116	  `variational_heat_envelope_paper` and `variational_global_mean_paper`;
   117	  the latter's first sentence (all mixed derivatives bounded) is not
   118	  formalized. `L:phase-bessel` is proved for any measure space and any
   119	  complete complex inner product space and stated with the manuscript's
   120	  hypotheses by `phase_bessel_paper` (separability carried and not used).
   121	  Three further results are formalized
   122	  with every conclusion proved but with analytic inputs supplied as named
   123	  hypotheses: `P:radius-mean-anchor` (the moment bound of
   124	  `C:radius-covariance-residuals`, and measurability of the Holder norm of

  2362	## PhaseBessel (whole result)
  2363	
  2364	Formalizes `L:phase-bessel` (Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality) of
  2365	`S:wave-variance` (`notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at `975feb3`:
  2366	statement lines 346-355 with the display `E:phase-bessel` at lines 350-353,
  2367	proof lines 357-366). The lemma cites no labels, and the section's standing
  2368	assumptions (lines 5-8: `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`) are not
  2369	used by it and are not carried. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The
  2370	general theorem `phase_bessel` holds for any measure space `(X, mu)` (no
  2371	sigma-finiteness), any complete complex inner product space `H` (no
  2372	separability) and any finite index types `iota` (the family index `k`) and
  2373	`J` (the vector index `j`; the TeX has `J = {1,2}`); `phase_bessel_paper`
  2374	states the TeX's hypotheses exactly: `X = R^d` (`EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)`)
  2375	with Lebesgue measure `volume`, `J = Fin 2`, a family indexed by `Fin K`, and
  2376	`H` separable. The spaces `L^2(R^d; C^2)` and `L^2(R^d; H^2)` are encoded
  2377	componentwise: each `u k j` and each `g j` is `MemLp 2` (this includes the
  2378	measurability the TeX leaves implicit), and orthonormality is the integral
  2379	identity `int sum_j u k j(eta) conj(u l j(eta)) d eta = delta_kl`
  2380	(`IsOrthonormalL2`), which is the TeX's `L^2(C^2)` inner product. Convention
  2381	remark: Mathlib's inner product `inner C x y` is conjugate-linear in the
  2382	FIRST slot, while the TeX's `<u_k, u_l> = int sum_j u_kj conj(u_lj)` is
  2383	linear in the first slot. Orthonormality is stated as the explicit integral
  2384	above, so no Mathlib inner product on `L^2` enters the hypothesis, and the
  2385	inequality (a statement about norms) does not depend on the convention.
  2386	The integral in `IsOrthonormalL2` cannot be a junk `0`, since its integrand
  2387	is integrable for `L^2` components (`integrable_mul_of_memLp`). The TeX's
  2388	"The Bochner integrals exist" is part of the conclusion: integrability of
  2389	every coefficient integrand `eta -> sum_j u k j(eta) g j(eta)` and of
  2390	`eta -> sum_j ||g j(eta)||^2`. Carried but unused: separability of `H`
  2391	(`_hsep` in `phase_bessel_paper`). Proof route (differs from the TeX): the
  2392	TeX expands `g` in a countable orthonormal basis of `H` (this is where it uses
  2393	separability), applies scalar Bessel coefficientwise and sums with Parseval
  2394	and Tonelli. Lean runs the projection argument that the TeX uses for scalar
  2395	Bessel directly in `H`: with `x_k = coeff mu u g k` and
  2396	`phi_j(eta) = sum_k conj(u k j(eta)) x_k`,
  2397	`0 <= int sum_j ||g_j - phi_j||^2 = int sum_j ||g_j||^2 - 2S + S`,
  2398	`S = sum_k ||x_k||^2` (`residual_expand`), so no basis, Parseval or
  2399	separability is needed. The conjugated version follows because the
  2400	componentwise conjugate family is orthonormal (`isOrthonormalL2_conj`). No
  2401	conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. Not formalized: the rest of
  2402	`S:wave-variance` (see "Not in Lean"); in particular `L:phase-bessel` is not
  2403	applied to `P:wave-two-variances` in Lean. Rows labelled "no direct label
  2404	(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

     1	\section{Frequency estimates and both wave variance directions}
     2	\label{S:wave-variance}
     3	
     4	We now apply the covariance and temporal estimates of
     5	Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance} to the full wave phase. We retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, write $a = \alpha_0$, and choose and fix
     7	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-gamma-range}
     8	  0 < \gamma < \min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right).
     9	\end{equation}
    10	The interval is nonempty because $\alpha+a < 2$. We use $\langle\xi\rangle =
    11	\sqrt{1+|\xi|^2}$ and set
    12	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-scale-profile}
    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\
    17	    h^{1-\alpha}, & \alpha > 1,
    18	  \end{cases}
    19	  \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    20	\end{equation}
    21	
    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
   330	  multiplication with the conjugate yields
   331	  \[
   332	    \widehat{F}_{z,w}(t,-\lambda)
   333	    = c_d1_I(t)\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2\mathcal{K}_{ij}(t;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   334	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta.
   335	  \]
   336	  The spatial integral is absolutely convergent uniformly on the finite time
   337	  interval by Schwartz decay. The Schur bound also makes it a Bochner
   338	  $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ integral. Reflect $\lambda$ using evenness of $\nu_R$
   339	  in~\eqref{E:variance-complex-noise}. Since $(2\pi)^dc_d^2 = 1$, this
   340	  proves~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} with no remaining Fourier
   341	  factor. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}.
   342	\end{proof}
   343	
   344	\subsection{Bessel's inequality and the two variances}
   345	
   346	\begin{lemma}[Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality]\label{L:phase-bessel}
   347	  Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $\{u_k\}$ be a finite
   348	  orthonormal family in $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$, and let $g = (g_1,g_2) \in
   349	  L^2(\R^d;H^2)$. Then
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-bessel}
   351	    \sum_k\left\|\int\sum_{j=1}^2u_{k,j}(\eta)g_j(\eta)\ud\eta\right\|_H^2
   352	    \le \int\sum_{j=1}^2\|g_j(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   353	  \end{equation}
   354	  The same bound holds with $\overline{u_{k,j}}$ in place of $u_{k,j}$.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Expand $g$ in a countable orthonormal basis of $H$. On each scalar coefficient
   359	  apply scalar Bessel to the orthonormal family $\{\overline{u_k}\}$, or to
   360	  $\{u_k\}$ for the conjugated version. Scalar finite Bessel follows by
   361	  subtracting an orthogonal finite projection and expanding its nonnegative
   362	  squared norm. Sum over the $H$ basis and use Parseval and nonnegative Tonelli.
   363	  The Bochner integrals exist by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. A finite-dimensional $H$
   364	  uses its finite basis, and the zero space is immediate. No independence is
   365	  involved. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}.
   366	\end{proof}
   367	
   368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}

  2362	## PhaseBessel (whole result)
  2363	
  2364	Formalizes `L:phase-bessel` (Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality) of
  2365	`S:wave-variance` (`notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at `975feb3`:
  2366	statement lines 346-355 with the display `E:phase-bessel` at lines 350-353,
  2367	proof lines 357-366). The lemma cites no labels, and the section's standing
  2368	assumptions (lines 5-8: `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`) are not
  2369	used by it and are not carried. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The
  2370	general theorem `phase_bessel` holds for any measure space `(X, mu)` (no
  2371	sigma-finiteness), any complete complex inner product space `H` (no
  2372	separability) and any finite index types `iota` (the family index `k`) and
  2373	`J` (the vector index `j`; the TeX has `J = {1,2}`); `phase_bessel_paper`
  2374	states the TeX's hypotheses exactly: `X = R^d` (`EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)`)
  2375	with Lebesgue measure `volume`, `J = Fin 2`, a family indexed by `Fin K`, and
  2376	`H` separable. The spaces `L^2(R^d; C^2)` and `L^2(R^d; H^2)` are encoded
  2377	componentwise: each `u k j` and each `g j` is `MemLp 2` (this includes the
  2378	measurability the TeX leaves implicit), and orthonormality is the integral
  2379	identity `int sum_j u k j(eta) conj(u l j(eta)) d eta = delta_kl`
  2380	(`IsOrthonormalL2`), which is the TeX's `L^2(C^2)` inner product. Convention
  2381	remark: Mathlib's inner product `inner C x y` is conjugate-linear in the
  2382	FIRST slot, while the TeX's `<u_k, u_l> = int sum_j u_kj conj(u_lj)` is
  2383	linear in the first slot. Orthonormality is stated as the explicit integral
  2384	above, so no Mathlib inner product on `L^2` enters the hypothesis, and the
  2385	inequality (a statement about norms) does not depend on the convention.
  2386	The integral in `IsOrthonormalL2` cannot be a junk `0`, since its integrand
  2387	is integrable for `L^2` components (`integrable_mul_of_memLp`). The TeX's
  2388	"The Bochner integrals exist" is part of the conclusion: integrability of
  2389	every coefficient integrand `eta -> sum_j u k j(eta) g j(eta)` and of
  2390	`eta -> sum_j ||g j(eta)||^2`. Carried but unused: separability of `H`
  2391	(`_hsep` in `phase_bessel_paper`). Proof route (differs from the TeX): the
  2392	TeX expands `g` in a countable orthonormal basis of `H` (this is where it uses
  2393	separability), applies scalar Bessel coefficientwise and sums with Parseval
  2394	and Tonelli. Lean runs the projection argument that the TeX uses for scalar
  2395	Bessel directly in `H`: with `x_k = coeff mu u g k` and
  2396	`phi_j(eta) = sum_k conj(u k j(eta)) x_k`,
  2397	`0 <= int sum_j ||g_j - phi_j||^2 = int sum_j ||g_j||^2 - 2S + S`,
  2398	`S = sum_k ||x_k||^2` (`residual_expand`), so no basis, Parseval or
  2399	separability is needed. The conjugated version follows because the
  2400	componentwise conjugate family is orthonormal (`isOrthonormalL2_conj`). No
  2401	conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. Not formalized: the rest of
  2402	`S:wave-variance` (see "Not in Lean"); in particular `L:phase-bessel` is not
  2403	applied to `P:wave-two-variances` in Lean. Rows labelled "no direct label
  2404	(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

  1285	## FrequencyRow (whole result)
  1286	
  1287	Formalizes Proposition `P:frequency-row` (lines 47-139) and Corollary
  1288	`C:frequency-time` (lines 141-165) of `notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at
  1289	`975feb3` (the file is byte-identical at `ba01d98`, so the line numbers hold
  1290	for both revisions). It also formalizes the definitions `E:variance-scale-profile`
  1291	(lines 12-20), `E:frequency-row-kernel` (lines 33-37) and
  1292	`E:frequency-row-integral` (lines 38-42), and the closed-ball remark after
  1293	`E:frequency-translated-growth` (lines 29-31). `bracket` and `frequencyPair`
  1294	(`Q_h` of `E:masked-frequency-pair`) are reused from `MaskedTrigProducts`.
  1295	`J_h(xi)` is a lower Lebesgue integral in `[0, inf]`, the "nonnegative
  1296	extended integral" of line 43, so no Bochner junk value enters its
  1297	definition. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.
  1298	
  1299	The quantifier order is exactly `exists K, forall d nu C h xi`. `frequency_row`
  1300	proves `exists K >= 0, forall d (nu a measure on R^d) C, C >= 0 -> growth -> forall h,
  1301	0 < h -> h <= 1 ->` `sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h)`. It also proves, for each
  1302	`xi`, `nu`-integrability of `lambda -> Phi_h(xi, xi-lambda)` and the real-integral
  1303	bound `<xi>^(2 gamma) int Phi_h(xi,xi-lambda) nu(dlambda) <= K C B_alpha(h)`
  1304	(the finiteness at lines 136-137). Its hypotheses are `a < 1`,
  1305	`alpha + a < 2`, `2 gamma <= 1` and `alpha + 2 gamma < 2`. The section's
  1306	range `0 < gamma < min(1/2, (2-alpha)/2)` (`E:variance-gamma-range`, lines 7-9)
  1307	implies the last two. `frequency_time` has the same form,
  1308	`exists K_beta >= 0, forall d nu C h`, with the extra hypotheses
  1309	`2 beta < 2 - a` and `2 beta < 3 - a - alpha`. The `_paper` wrappers take the
  1310	section's hypotheses: `H:homog` with `a = alpha0` as
  1311	`HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu` (lines 5-6), the range of `gamma`, a
  1312	locally finite (Radon) `nu`, `C >= 0` and the growth bound. The corollary also
  1313	takes `1/2 < beta < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-alpha)/2)` (`E:variance-beta-range`,
  1314	lines 143-145). In the wrappers the constant is chosen before
  1315	`d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h` (and `xi`).
  1316	
  1317	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `B(y,r)` in
  1318	`E:frequency-translated-growth` is read as the open ball, the weaker
  1319	hypothesis, and `closedBall_le` derives the closed-ball bound. `nu` is a
  1320	measure on the Borel sigma-algebra. Measurability of the kernel is proved,
  1321	not assumed. Integrability is part of the conclusion.
  1322	
  1323	Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): `gamma > 0`, `beta > 1/2`, local
  1324	finiteness of `nu`, and all of `H:homog` except `alpha0 < 1` and
  1325	`alpha0 + alpha < 2`. The general theorems hold for every `d`, including
  1326	`d = 0`, and every real `alpha` meeting their numerical hypotheses.
  1327	
  1328	Proof route. The integrand is bounded pointwise by two dyadic shell
  1329	majorants of closed balls of radius `2^j`: one around `xi` on the near region
  1330	`|lambda| <= 4|xi|`, one around `0` on the far region. The TeX splits at
  1331	`4q`, `q = max(1,|xi|)`. On the near region `<xi> >= 2^n/5` gives the single
  1332	ratio `2^(alpha+2gamma-2) < 1` for all three cases of `alpha`. This replaces
  1333	the three-case bound on `A_xi(q)` (lines 60-99). The far region and the

  1335	`h 2^M > 1`, which is `L + 1` of line 121. The corollary follows lines

   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215	
   216	Throughout we write
   217	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   218	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   219	\end{equation}
   220	
   221	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   222	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   223	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   224	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   225	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   226	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   227	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   228	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   229	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   230	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   231	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   232	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   233	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   361	## DimensionalMatrix
   362	
   363	Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
   364	interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
   365	unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
   366	the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
   367	`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
   368	`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
   369	`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
   370	`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
   371	kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
   372	(`L:masked-continuous-wave`; defined in Lean as `MaskedContinuousWave.bFn`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
   373	change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
   374	`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
   375	zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
   376	are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
   377	`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in
   378	`L:symplectic-free`, which also defines the force `B(b)`.
   379

   382	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.backward` | Definition: `[[cp, -sp/p], [p sp, cp]]`, the backward free matrix `S(-t)` at one frequency. | The interpretation of `cp, sp` as cosine and sine of a phase, and the continuous extension at zero frequency. |
   383	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.coupling` | Definition: `[[0, 0], [H, 0]]`, the force `B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)` with `H` for `b`. | The meaning of `H` as a covariance coefficient. |
   384	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward` | Definition: `[[cq, sq/q], [-q sq, cq]]`, the free matrix `S(t)` at one frequency. | As for `backward`. |
   385	| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.full_interaction` | For all real parameters (field division), `backward * coupling * forward = [[-(sp/p) H cq, -(sp/p) H (sq/q)], [cp H cq, cp H (sq/q)]]`, the unweighted product `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` at fixed frequencies. | The Bessel-weighted coordinate change and the weight `1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)` that turn it into `E:variance-normalized-kernel`; Fourier multiplication and covariance integrals; the zero-frequency case. |

  6773	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/phase-bessel-is-orthonormal-l2
  6774	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.PhaseBessel.IsOrthonormalL2
  6775	  kind: definition
  6776	  summary: "Orthonormality of a finite family u : iota -> J -> X -> C in L^2(X; C^J) for a measure mu: every u k j is in L^2(mu), and int sum_j u k j * conj(u l j) dmu = 1 if k = l, else 0 (inner product linear in the first slot)."
  6777	  keywords: [orthonormal-family, l2-space]
  6778	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
  6779	  status: reusable
  6780	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/phase-bessel-coeff
  6781	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.PhaseBessel.coeff
  6782	  kind: definition
  6783	  summary: "The k-th coefficient vector coeff mu u g k = int sum_j u k j(eta) * g j(eta) dmu(eta) in H, a Bochner integral (the vector inside the norm on the left of E:phase-bessel)."
  6784	  keywords: [bochner-integral, bessel-coefficient]
  6785	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
  6786	  status: reusable
  6787	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/phase-bessel-mem-lp-conj
  6788	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.PhaseBessel.memLp_conj
  6789	  kind: theorem
  6790	  summary: "For any measure mu and f : X -> C in L^2(mu), the conjugate eta -> conj(f eta) is in L^2(mu)."
  6791	  keywords: [l2-space, complex-conjugate]
  6792	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
  6793	  status: internal
  6794	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/phase-bessel-integrable-mul-of-mem-lp
  6795	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.PhaseBessel.integrable_mul_of_memLp
  6796	  kind: theorem
  6797	  summary: "For any measure mu and f, h : X -> C in L^2(mu), the product eta -> f eta * h eta is mu-integrable."
  6798	  keywords: [l2-space, holder-inequality]
  6799	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
  6800	  status: internal

  6803	  kind: theorem
  6804	  summary: "For any measure mu, f : X -> C in L^2(mu) and h : X -> H in L^2(mu) (H a complex inner product space), eta -> f eta * h eta is Bochner integrable."
  6805	  keywords: [bochner-integral, holder-inequality]
  6806	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
  6807	  status: internal
  6808	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/phase-bessel-integrable-coeff-integrand

  6811	  summary: "For any measure mu, J finite, every u k j : X -> C in L^2(mu) and every g j : X -> H in L^2(mu): for each k, eta -> sum_j u k j(eta) * g j(eta) is Bochner integrable."
  6812	  keywords: [bochner-integral, l2-space]
  6813	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/PhaseBessel.lean
